haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 and stops. No counter is read or changed, and Redis is never called.
haiku-low.q2: Standard is 100 per minute total. All of a customer's keys share one counter per minute, so the three keys share one budget.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After in whole seconds. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. A rejected 429 changes nothing, so it uses no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. Once the check passes, the request stays counted even if the backend returns 500.
haiku-low.q6: The gateway fails open: it forwards the request, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and omits the X-RateLimit-* headers.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 requests per minute. Enterprise is not decided, so its limit is TBD and cannot be enforced yet.
haiku-low.q8: In shared Redis, under key ratelimit:{customerId}:{minute}. A TTL of 120 seconds on the key removes old counts.
haiku-low.q9: At the start of each new clock minute the count resets to 0. It is a fixed window, so there is no gradual recovery.
haiku-low.q10: The check_and_incr Lua script runs as one indivisible Redis step, so two instances cannot both pass the last unit.
haiku-low.q11: 60 minus the seconds already elapsed in the current minute, as whole seconds, with a minimum of 1.
haiku-low.q12: Retry behaviour is NOT STATED. The client gets no X-RateLimit-Limit or X-RateLimit-Remaining headers.

sonnet.q1: It gets a 401 and processing stops. Redis is never called, so no counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: Counters are per customer, not per key, so all three keys share one budget. The total is the customer's plan limit per minute (Standard 100 per minute; Enterprise TBD).
sonnet.q3: The client gets 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (in seconds). The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
sonnet.q4: No. The script returns 'rejected' and changes nothing, so a 429 uses no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. It counts against the budget even though the backend failed.
sonnet.q6: The gateway fails open. It forwards the request to the backend, emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, and leaves out the X-RateLimit-* headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 requests per minute. Enterprise is not decided (TBD), so the gateway cannot enforce an Enterprise limit yet.
sonnet.q8: In Redis, shared by all 6 gateway instances, under the counter key ratelimit:{customerId}:{minute}. A TTL of 120 seconds, set on the first add in a window, makes Redis delete old keys.
sonnet.q9: Budget resets when the next clock minute starts. It is a fixed window, and each new window's counter starts at 0.
sonnet.q10: The Lua script check_and_incr runs in Redis as one indivisible step (atomic check-and-count). Two instances therefore cannot both pass on the last unit of budget.
sonnet.q11: It is the whole seconds until the current minute ends: 60 minus the seconds already elapsed, with a minimum of 1.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED whether the gateway retries the store. The request is simply forwarded. The client gets no X-RateLimit-Limit or X-RateLimit-Remaining headers, because the count is unknown.
